entry.title: Gary Stevenson's inequality documentary: capitalism indicted, but is a wealth tax enough?
entry.summary: As an indictment of British capitalism the documentary is excellent. The trouble starts with the remedy: £24 billion is roughly one week of government spending.

entry.title: The Chinese revolutions of 1927 and 1949
entry.summary: A leadoff written for a CWI summer school. Two revolutions, one question: at each stage, what would you have done as a Marxist standing there, with the information available at the time?

entry.title: Gaza, Lebanon and the anti-war movement
entry.summary: Eight pieces written for the Socialist across two and a half years of the war, from the first mass demonstrations in London to the assault on Lebanon. Collected here in reverse order.

entry.title: Marxist economics: the state of the world economy
entry.summary: A leadoff on the world economy. Everything that caused 2008 is still there, and four things have been added since: two major wars, a US-China trade war, protectionism, and sixteen years of low investment.

entry.title: Trump's war on the climate
entry.summary: Rescinding the endangerment finding would strip the legal basis from US climate regulation. Behind it lies a tactical shift, not a break with what the Democrats did before.

entry.title: China: state intervention, world economic crisis and class struggle
entry.summary: An introduction to the discussion on China at Socialism 2025. A Bonapartist state that bred its own capitalist class, and what happens to it when the growth that held the arrangement together runs out.

entry.title: China's revolutionary tragedy
entry.summary: Why, despite the courage and determination of the masses, the revolution in China that began one hundred years ago ended in defeat.

entry.title: Capitalist climate hypocrisy: who should pay for the crisis?
entry.summary: Guyana's president asks the BBC a fair question. If the West values the forest, is it willing to pay for it? The answer exposes what a market cannot do.

entry.title: Defeating imperialist intervention
entry.summary: A review of Anna Reid's A Nasty Little War. Meticulously researched, politically bereft: it cannot explain why 180,000 imperialist troops lost.

entry.title: The US must do more to combat carbon inequality in the global economy
entry.summary: Winning entry in the LSE Phelan US Centre climate change essay competition. National emissions accounts are the wrong unit: responsibility sits with the corporations and investors who own the emissions, and most of them are American.
